markings.notes: dusky stripe; the lateral line dips steeply down toward the belly and levels off to the tail
gold in tannin-dark water, silver in clear water

pattern.fins: often tinted reddish-orange; anal fin crescent-shaped; scaleless keel along the belly between pelvic fins and vent; small upturned mouth

variants.spawning_male: breeding colours not described in the sources used; keep adult colours with the warmest fin tint
variants.juvenile: silver, with herringbone lines on the upper side

pattern.source: FishBase short description; Lazur and Chapman 1996; Florida Springs Institute

regulations.notes: Nongame fish: no bag or length limit. Cast nets for bait in fresh water: stretched mesh no greater than 1 in; minnow traps up to 24 in long. Taking bait for sale needs a commercial licence.

economy.notes: Not a food fish. Its value is as live bait (wild shiners for big bass); handle through the bait economy.

facts: Golden shiners tolerate water up to 40 C, the highest temperature of any North American minnow.
They sense 'schreckstoff', the alarm substance of injured minnows, and in one study avoided places marked by the droppings of snakes that had eaten shiners.
A female scatters 10,000-20,000 sticky eggs over submerged plants, early in the morning, several times a season.

research.task: Catch one on a pinch of bread on a tiny hook
Catch three from the same school without spooking it
Catch a Florida bass on a shiner you caught yourself

ledger.wrenNote: Tiny hook, a pea of bread, no weight. Flick a few crumbs out first and wait for the flash under them. Keep the ones you catch cool and lively. A big bass can tell.
